analysis:
The PR only changes docs/architecture/inference.md. The diff adds head lines 595-611, which describe a Gated DeltaNet four-row prefill kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. This is documentation only, with no code, config, endpoint or deployment changes.

The supplied units (head lines 802-1643) are surrounding, unchanged text, so they show no change in security behavior. I examined the surrounding sections: prefix cache, deadlines, MTP, media caps, tool parsers and sampling. The relevant unchanged contracts include T-041 and TB-007 for the SSD prefix cache and the TTFT oracle, and T-008 and T-010 for fail-closed encryption and cancellation. Nothing in these units asserts a new control or weakens an existing one.

The new kernel text claims two things. Kernel selection is a per-process probe, and the packed or rows kernel is kept only if it reproduces gated_delta_step bit for bit, otherwise the stock kernel runs. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and windows shorter than 16 positions always use the stock kernel, so recurrent state captured in checkpoints is unaffected. If the claim holds, the implementation does not change the prefix-cache state or checkpoint identity covered by T-041. A new env var, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED, only chooses the stock kernel or forces packed or rows for A/B measurement.

The implementing code is not in this batch: GatedDelta.swift and GatedDeltaPrefill. I could not verify that the bit-exactness probe is sound, or that forcing a kernel through the env var cannot yield state that differs across chunks. Any such difference would only affect output correctness or cache-state determinism, which is not a confidentiality regression on its own. A later review of the code change, if one exists, should check the probe and the forced-kernel path. No security regression is identified from this documentation diff.
